notes.deenhindi-tirmidhi:2683: Both entire originals independently read. Yazid supplies his actual hearing/forgetting concern and the given reply about what he knows. Hindi has a damaged concern/request join and does not supply Urdu's complete request; preserve that own fragment and reply without completion. The beginning/end parenthesis supplies the source's two-part scope and may remain qualified; Urdu's kalimah/something-to-say parenthesis is a duplicate lexical rendering. Urdu's numbered locator and compiler comments about discontinuity, Ibn-Ashwa not meeting Yazid and the name definition are source-critical apparatus.
notes.deenhindi-tirmidhi:2690: Both long originals independently read completely. Abu Said reports the actual three requests, Umar's internal counts, return/recall, challenge, Abu Musa's visit to the Ansar, the expressly cited Prophetic permission report, the group's reaction, Abu Said's response and the final reporting to Umar. Keep all distinct voices/components and the embedded conditional permission instruction. The in-the-heart parentheses materially distinguish thought from spoken replies; further specifies the repeated wait; hearing-this gives the reaction relation; the final Abu-Said parenthesis supplies the later he referent. Retain these as source-rendered narration. The permission-seeking parenthesis supplies the subject of the source's translated three-times clause alongside the actual Arabic quote, so retain that reported translation rather than reducing it to an orphaned predicate. Urdu's locator, grading, names and route/bab notices remain context. No external scene or attribution is added.
notes.deenhindi-tirmidhi:2694: Both entire originals independently read. Abu Umamah supplies the passive question about two people meeting and who initiates the greeting, then the nearer-to-Allah reply. The parenthetic he-will-initiate completes the source-rendered action/subject relation in that reply and should remain qualified, without asserting verbatim wording across languages. Keep the two-person condition and actual attribution. The appended Tirmidhi/Bukhari grading and father/son narrator criticism are transmission apparatus, not additional narrated sayings to promote.
